- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

content.text:
I have enough to answer definitively.

r05.

**Premise correction:** There is no GraphQL schema in this repository. This is the Memos project (`module github.com/usememos/memos`, `go.mod:1`), and its public API is **not** GraphQL. A repo-wide search for "graphql" across Go, JSON, mod, and Markdown files returns zero matches.

**Actual API surface:** The public API is defined with **Protocol Buffers** and served over **gRPC / Connect**, with a generated **REST/OpenAPI** gateway. Specifically:

- **Schema definitions (source of truth):** `proto/api/v1/` — one `.proto` file per service:
  - `proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`
  - `proto/api/v1/user_service.proto`
  - `proto/api/v1/auth_service.proto`
  - `proto/api/v1/attachment_service.proto`
  - `proto/api/v1/ai_service.proto`
  - `proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto`
  - `proto/api/v1/instance_service.proto`
  - `proto/api/v1/shortcut_service.proto`
  - `proto/api/v1/common.proto`
- **Build/codegen config:** `proto/buf.yaml`, `proto/buf.gen.yaml`, `proto/buf.lock` (uses [buf](https://buf.build); see `proto/README.md`).
- **Generated code + OpenAPI spec:** `proto/gen/` — including `proto/gen/openapi.yaml` (the generated REST/OpenAPI surface) and the embedding helper `proto/openapi_embed.go`.
- **Server-side API implementation:** the `server/` directory wires these services up.

So the correct answer to "where is the API schema defined" is the protobuf files under `proto/api/v1/`, exposed as gRPC/Connect endpoints plus a REST/OpenAPI gateway — there is no GraphQL layer.

<result>I have a thorough and complete picture. Here are my findings.

## GraphQL: None found

There is **zero GraphQL usage** in this repository. I checked exhaustively:
- No `.graphql`, `.gql`, or `.graphqls` files exist.
- No `graphql`, `apollo`, `urql`, `relay-runtime` references in any source, config, YAML, proto, or markdown file (case-insensitive sweep across the whole repo excluding `.git`).
- `/bench/repo/web/package.json` has no GraphQL/Apollo/urql client — the only API clients are `@connectrpc/connect` and `@connectrpc/connect-web`.
- `/bench/repo/go.mod` contains no GraphQL server library.

This is the **Memos** project (`github.com/usememos/memos`), a Go backend with a TypeScript/React web frontend.

## Actual public API surface

The API is **Protobuf-defined, exposed simultaneously as gRPC, Connect RPC, and REST (via grpc-gateway)** — plus several auxiliary HTTP endpoints.

### 1. Protobuf service definitions (source of truth)
Located in `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/`:
- `memo_service.proto`
- `user_service.proto`
- `auth_service.proto`
- `attachment_service.proto`
- `shortcut_service.proto`
- `instance_service.proto`
- `ai_service.proto`
- `idp_service.proto`
- `common.proto`

Store-layer protos in `/bench/repo/proto/store/` (persistence models: `memo.proto`, `user_setting.proto`, `inbox.proto`, `idp.proto`, `attachment.proto`, `instance_setting.proto`).

Build config: `/bench/repo/proto/buf.yaml`, `/bench/repo/proto/buf.gen.yaml`, `/bench/repo/proto/buf.lock`.

### 2. Generated API stubs — `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/`
Three transports are generated from the same protos:
- **gRPC**: `*_grpc.pb.go` files
- **REST/JSON gateway**: `*.pb.gw.go` files (grpc-gateway v2 — HTTP/JSON REST endpoints)
- **Connect RPC**: `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/*.connect.go` (e.g. `memo_service.connect.go`, `auth_service.connect.go`, etc.)

### 3. OpenAPI
- `/bench/repo/proto/gen/openapi.yaml` — generated OpenAPI/Swagger spec for the REST surface.
- `/bench/repo/proto/openapi_embed.go` — embeds that spec into the binary.

### 4. Server wiring — `/bench/repo/server/server.go`
Single Echo (`labstack/echo/v5`) HTTP server (all traffic is HTTP, no cmux). It mounts:
- **grpc-gateway REST + Connect handlers** via `apiV1Service.RegisterGateway()` — see `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (line 65). Connect handlers are implemented in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go` (a `ConnectServiceHandler` delegating to the gRPC implementations). SSE endpoint is also registered here.
- **REST service implementations** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/` (e.g. `memo_service.go`, `user_service.go`, `auth_service.go`, `attachment_service.go`, `ai_service.go`, `idp_service.go`, `reaction_service.go`, plus helpers).
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol) server**: `/bench/repo/server/router/mcp/` (`service.go`, `catalog.go`, `adapter.go`, `openapi.go`) — uses `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`. This is a notable additional public API surface exposing memos as MCP tools/resources.
- **RSS feed**: `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`
- **File server** (native HTTP for range requests / video/audio): `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`
- **Frontend static file server**: `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go`
- **Healthz**: `GET /healthz` (in `server.go`).

### 5. Web frontend client
`/bench/repo/web/` — React app consuming the API via **Connect** (`@connectrpc/connect`, `@connectrpc/connect-web`). Generated TS types live in `/bench/repo/web/src/types/proto/api/v1/` (and `.../google/...`), mirroring the protobuf definitions.

### Summary
The public API is **not REST-first, tRPC, or GraphQL** — it is a **Protobuf/gRPC contract surfaced as gRPC + Connect RPC + REST (grpc-gateway) with a generated OpenAPI spec**, complemented by MCP, RSS, and static/file-serving HTTP endpoints. The frontend talks to it over Connect.</result>
